title: Maximum Number of Points with Cost
statement:
You are given an `m x n` integer grid `points`. Choose exactly one cell in every row. Your score is the sum of `points[r][c]` over the chosen cells, minus a penalty for each pair of consecutive rows: if the cell chosen in row `r` is in column `c1` and the cell chosen in row `r + 1` is in column `c2`, you lose `|c1 - c2|`.

Return the largest score you can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

Let `prev[k]` be the best score of the rows so far that ends in column `k`. The next row's cell in column `c` should add `max over k of (prev[k] - |k - c|)`. Trying every `k` (the brute force) costs O(n²) per row. Split the absolute value instead: for `k <= c` the term is `prev[k] - (c - k)`, a running maximum that loses 1 per step to the right; for `k >= c` it is the mirror image. Two sweeps give every column's best predecessor in O(n).

## Approach

1. Start `prev` as a copy of the first row.
2. For each later row `r`, sweep left to right: `fromLeft[c] = max(fromLeft[c - 1] - 1, prev[c])`, the best `prev[k] - (c - k)` with `k <= c`.
3. Sweep right to left the same way to fill `fromRight[c]`, the best for `k >= c`.
4. `current[c] = points[r][c] + max(fromLeft[c], fromRight[c])`; then `current` becomes `prev`.
5. Return the largest value of `prev` after the last row.

## Example 1, step by step

`prev = [1, 2, 3]`. Row 1: `fromLeft = [1, 2, 3]`, `fromRight = [1, 2, 3]` (3 - 1 = 2 ties with 2), so `current = [1 + 1, 5 + 2, 1 + 3] = [2, 7, 4]`. Row 2: `fromLeft = [2, 7, 6]`, `fromRight = [6, 7, 4]`, so `current = [3 + 6, 1 + 7, 1 + 6] = [9, 8, 7]`. The answer is `9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): three linear passes per row.
- Space: O(n): a few arrays as wide as one row.

## Pitfalls

- The O(m · n²) double loop is too slow when one row has 10^5 cells.
- `fromLeft[c - 1] - 1` already carries the distance: moving one column further costs exactly one more point, so no explicit `|k - c|` is needed.
- Scores reach about 10^10, beyond 32-bit integers; Java needs `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prev` | best score ending at each column of the previous row |
| `fromLeft[c]` | best `prev[k] - (c - k)` over `k <= c` |
| `fromRight[c]` | best `prev[k] - (k - c)` over `k >= c` |
| `current` | best score ending at each column of row `r` |
| `cols` | number of columns |

narration.3: With only the first row picked, the best score in each column is the cell itself.
narration.4: Add the remaining rows one at a time.
narration.6: Column 0 has nothing to its left, so its best predecessor is prev[0].
narration.8: Either keep the best from the left, now one column further away, or start from prev[c] itself.
narration.12: Sweep right to left for predecessors on the right side.
narration.13: Same rule mirrored: the right-side best loses one point per step.
narration.16: Each cell of this row takes the better of the two sides.
narration.17: Add the cell's own points to the best predecessor score.
narration.19: This row becomes the previous row for the next step.
narration.21: The answer is the best score in any column of the last row.
